That precaution did not establish an Iranian missile impact there. Qatar called for military action to stop and for a return to dialogue.

title: Trump Directs Dismissal of Pending January 6 Indictments on Inauguration Day
short_description: Trump’s January 20, 2025 proclamation directed the attorney general to seek dismissal of pending January 6 indictments with prejudice.
medium_description: On January 20, 2025, Trump directed the attorney general to pursue dismissal with prejudice of pending indictments involving conduct at or near the Capitol on January 6, 2021. long_description:
President Donald Trump issued a proclamation on January 20, 2025, directing the attorney general to pursue dismissal with prejudice of pending indictments for conduct related to the events at or near the Capitol on January 6, 2021. The directive formed part of an inauguration-day clemency action recorded on the Justice Department’s list of second-term grants.

The proclamation separately commuted the sentences of fourteen named individuals to time served and pardoned other people convicted of offenses connected to those events. It instructed the attorney general to issue pardon certificates and ensure the immediate release of covered prisoners. Its provision concerning pending cases directed prosecutors to pursue dismissals; the proclamation itself was not a court order disposing of every indictment.

The text defines the covered pending cases by their connection to January 6 conduct. It does not announce a blanket dismissal of every federal case against a Trump associate. The initiating action was Trump’s presidential proclamation. Pam Bondi’s appointment affidavit dates her appointment as attorney general to February 5, 2025, after this directive.
